title: Direction-balance changes retain bilateral covariance after pair and neuron scales cancel in three adult fly maps
abstract: We tested whether count changes between adult fly maps affect both directions of a neuron pair in the same way. We used matched ipsilateral connections from FlyWire FAFB v783, male CNS v1.0 and BANC v888. Each direction had at least 64 counts across four copies, and all eight counts were positive. After excluded-pair neuron gain fits, direction-balance changes had cross-side correlations of 0.310, 0.454 and 0.466 in 2,192, 592 and 677 pairs. We developed a graph test that removes all neuron input and output multipliers and any common pair multiplier from noiseless log count changes. This post hoc test retained cycle covariances of 0.00759, 0.00708 and 0.00475 in squared log-ratio units. Each exceeded all 200 fitted contact-only simulation values. The simulation preserved arbitrary pair totals, fitted neuron gains and count selection. Cycle correlations were 0.234, 0.373 and 0.306; the last lay within the simulated correlation range. Thus the tested scalar pair and neuron model does not explain all repeated direction changes under the count reference. Three animals and different pipelines cannot separate biology from shared reconstruction errors or direction-specific geometry. The package includes the proof, code, aggregate evidence, figures and exact external input hashes. No external record-level data are bundled.

display.caption: Direction-balance changes repeat across sides after neuron gain fits and exact removal of node gradients. Color bars are approximate 95% identity-weight intervals; grey bars span 200 contact-only simulations.
